name: Democratic People's Republic of Korea - Subnational Administrative Boundaries (COD-AB)
publisher: OCHA Regional Office for Asia and the Pacific (ROAP) / HDX
description: The standardized United Nations Common Operational Datasets for DPRK administrative levels 0 (country), 1 (11 provinces/special cities), and 2 (179 counties/cities). Features standard P-codes (KP01, KP0101, etc.) for direct linkage to humanitarian and demographic datasets.
last_updated_evidence: HDX API package last_modified timestamp is 2026-08-14T07:23:03; reviewed for accuracy October 31, 2024.
license: Creative Commons Attribution for Intergovernmental Organisations (CC BY-IGO)
presentation: Clean downloadable shapefile, geodatabase, geojson and xlsx. However, it is published as raw GIS downloads with no interactive web map on HDX.
build_idea: Use as the primary administrative boundary layer for county-level choropleths (population density, night lights, crop stress, and defector origins) across the entire platform.
notes: Admin 2 includes 179 units. Two Admin 2 units in COD-AB do not have matching tabular records in COD-PS due to minor 2008 census zoning differences, which can be cleanly bridged with a normalization lookup.

name: Democratic People's Republic of Korea - Subnational Population Statistics (COD-PS)
publisher: OCHA Regional Office for Asia and the Pacific (ROAP) / HDX
description: County and province population statistics from the 2008 DPRK census formatted specifically for database/GIS linkage to COD-AB boundaries. Provides total, male, female, urban, and rural population counts for all 179 Admin 2 units.
last_updated_evidence: HDX API metadata_modified timestamp is 2025-07-22T20:39:35; resource prk_pop_adm2_v2.csv verified via curl (180 lines, 23 KB).
license: Creative Commons Attribution for Intergovernmental Organisations (CC BY-IGO)
presentation: Tabular CSV and Excel files available on HDX; no visual presentation or mapping provided.
build_idea: Directly join to COD-AB GeoJSON polygons by ADM2_PCODE to render interactive county-level population and urbanization choropleths.
notes: Total enumerated civilian population across the 179 counties is 23,275,627 (excluding institutional military personnel in barracks of 702,372).

name: geoBoundaries DPRK Open Administrative Boundaries (ADM0-ADM2)
description: Openly licensed administrative boundary polygons for North Korea at ADM0 (country), ADM1 (provinces), and ADM2 (counties) maintained by the William & Mary geoLab. Provides standardized GeoJSON, TopoJSON, and Shapefile representations with consistent topology.
last_updated_evidence: API response from https://www.geoboundaries.org/api/current/gbOpen/PRK/ADM2/ verified; geoBoundaries release 9469f09 contains 179 features.
license: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0)
presentation: Available via REST API and GitHub raw files with lightweight GeoJSON suitable for direct web vector rendering.
build_idea: Use as a lightweight, un-zipped fallback GeoJSON for client-side MapLibre boundary overlays when OCHA geodatabases are too heavy.
notes: Properties include shapeName, shapeID, shapeGroup, and shapeType. English names are transliterated.

name: GADM DPRK Database of Global Administrative Areas (Levels 0-2)
description: High-resolution spatial database of administrative areas for North Korea covering country (Level 0), provinces (Level 1), and counties/cities (Level 2). Widely used in academic spatial econometrics and global species/climate modeling.
last_updated_evidence: GADM version 4.1 release date; file metadata verified via UCDavis geodata mirrors.
license: Non-commercial academic use (free for research and educational purposes)
presentation: Static downloads in GeoPackage, Shapefile, KMZ, and RDS formats.
build_idea: Secondary boundary verification to cross-check county boundary shifts and topological disputes against OCHA COD-AB.
notes: Non-commercial restriction requires care if public commercial redistributions ever occur; OCHA COD-AB and OSM are preferred for open-source sites.

name: Justin Elliot Meyers DPRK Administrative Boundary Shapefiles
description: Official DPRK administrative boundary shapefile reconstructed with Korean UFID identifiers and Hangul place names. Unlike UN datasets that group Pyongyang into one city, this dataset features 218 units detailing Pyongyang's municipal districts (낙랑구역, 만경대구역, 대동강구역, etc.) and provincial counties.
coverage: North Korea nationwide including municipal guyok
last_updated_evidence: GitHub repository commit date and binary DBF header inspection (218 records, fields UFID and NAME in UTF-8 Hangul).
license: unstated
presentation: Raw ESRI shapefiles hosted on GitHub with DBF attribute tables.
build_idea: Essential for high-resolution mapping of Pyongyang and major cities, where UN datasets only have one polygon but defector, market, and facility reports specify exact guyok (e.g. Moranbong-guyok).
notes: DBF records verified: contains Korean Hangul names like 낙랑구역, 대성구역, 옹진군, 강령군, 삼지연, etc.

name: OpenStreetMap DPRK Administrative Relations (Levels 4 & 6 via Overpass)
description: Community-maintained administrative boundary relations for North Korea with bilingual Korean (name:ko) and English (name:en) tagging. Contains 11 Level 4 relations (provinces/special cities) and 196 Level 6 relations (counties, cities, urban districts).
last_updated_evidence: Overpass API live response timestamped 2026-10-01T15:41:51Z; verified 196 Level 6 relations.
license: Open Data Commons Open Database License (ODbL 1.0)
presentation: Queryable via Overpass QL returning JSON or XML; visualizable in JOSM or web map editors.
build_idea: Provides bilingual Hangul/English names and live relation IDs that match our MapLibre base map perfectly without projection or alignment shifts.
notes: Counties like 삼지연시 reflect recent upgrades to 'City' (si) status made by the DPRK government.

name: Geofabrik OpenStreetMap North Korea Daily PBF Extract
description: Daily updated OpenStreetMap raw vector database extract covering the entire territory of North Korea. Includes all administrative boundary polygons, roads, railways, rivers, residential clusters, industrial complexes, and named settlements.
coverage: Daily rolling snapshot, North Korea nationwide
last_updated_evidence: Server HTTP headers indicate Last-Modified: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 23:55:22 GMT; Content-Length: 92,390,860 bytes.
license: Open Data Commons Open Database License (ODbL 1.0)
presentation: Raw compressed protobuf (.osm.pbf) file, 92 MB.
build_idea: Extract all boundary relations, town centroids (ri, dong, eup), and settlement areas with osmium/gdal to power autocomplete and boundary vector tiles.
notes: Download size is 92 MB, well within our 200 MB limit.

name: 2008 DPRK Population Census National Report & Digital Tables
publisher: Central Bureau of Statistics, Pyongyang & UNFPA
description: The official report of the 2008 National Population Census conducted October 1-15, 2008 across DPRK with UNFPA technical backing. Enumerated 24,052,231 citizens, providing county-level populations by sex and urban/rural status, and provincial-level 5-year age groups, marital status, education, and household amenities.
last_updated_evidence: Published in 2009 by Central Bureau of Statistics Pyongyang; digitized tabular dataset verified in prk_pop.xls (80,384 bytes).
license: Public domain / UN Official Publication
presentation: Original printed report scanned into PDF; key tabular sheets preserved in UN/HDX Excel workbooks.
build_idea: Foundational baseline for all North Korean demographic maps: county choropleths of sex ratio, urban percentage, and household density.
notes: This remains the only comprehensive census in North Korean history with verified county-level disaggregation. The 702,372 military personnel were enumerated separately and excluded from county totals.

name: UNFPA DPRK Country Programme: Planned 2018-2019 Census Documentation
description: Documentation and project files regarding the planned 2018-2019 DPRK Population and Housing Census. Tracks the initial preparations, pilot census, South Korea's planned $6 million funding via the Inter-Korean Cooperation Fund, and its subsequent cancellation due to international sanctions and border closures.
last_updated_evidence: UNFPA Executive Board country programme document DP/FPA/CPD/PRK/6 and related committee minutes.
license: UN Official Document
presentation: UN Executive Board reports and press briefs.
build_idea: Document the history and reasons why North Korea lacks a post-2008 census on our site's research & data-explainer page.
notes: Explains why all post-2008 national and county figures are econometric and demographic projections (UN WPP, Statistics Korea, WorldPop) rather than field census counts.

name: UN World Population Prospects (WPP 2024 Revision) Data Portal API
publisher: United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs, Population Division
description: Official programmatic REST API for global demographic estimates and projections from 1950 to 2100. Includes 108 indicators for DPRK (Location ID 408) including total population by sex, 5-year age cohorts, crude birth/death rates, total fertility rate, and life expectancy.
coverage: 1950-2100, DPRK national totals and age structures
last_updated_evidence: WPP 2024 Revision released July 2024; endpoint https://population.un.org/dataportalapi/api/v1/locations/408 verified via curl.
license: Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 IGO
presentation: Modern REST API and interactive web portal with chart visualizers.
build_idea: Drive national-level demographic timeline charts showing North Korea's population trajectory, aging pyramid, and historical mortality dips (1990s famine).
notes: Querying indicator data directly via dataportalapi requires a free bearer token generated from the developer portal UI, or direct downloads via the R wpp2024 package.

name: UN World Population Prospects (WPP 2024) Data Repository (PPgp/wpp2024)
publisher: UN Population Division & University of Washington
description: Complete raw open-source demographic datasets of the 2024 Revision of World Population Prospects. Contains annual and 5-year age-sex demographic tables for North Korea (country code 408) from 1950 to 2023 estimates and projections up to 2100.
last_updated_evidence: GitHub commits to PPgp/wpp2024 matching the official UN WPP 2024 release.
license: GPL-2 / CC BY 3.0 IGO
presentation: R data packages and text tables on GitHub.
build_idea: Extract pre-computed annual DPRK population and age-group breakdowns for offline bundling in the Next.js static build.
notes: Verified line in UNlocations.txt: 'Dem. People's Republic of Korea', code 408, Eastern Asia.

name: World Bank World Development Indicators (WDI) API - DPRK Population & Vital Rates
description: High-availability, keyless REST API providing annual time series of North Korea's total population, female/male ratios, urban population percentage, fertility, life expectancy, and dependency ratios from 1960 through 2025.
last_updated_evidence: Verified curl response returning values up to 2025 (26,571,036).
license: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 (CC BY 4.0)
presentation: JSON and XML REST API, cleanly formatted with no authentication required.
build_idea: Use in header stat cards and national overview summary widgets ('Total Population: 26.5M').
notes: Indicator codes: SP.POP.TOTL (population), SP.DYN.LE00.IN (life expectancy), SP.URB.TOTL.IN.ZS (urban pop %).

name: WorldPop North Korea 100m Constrained Population Raster (BSGM)
description: High-resolution 100m (3 arc-second) gridded population raster for North Korea for year 2020. Constrained using the Built-Settlement Growth Model (BSGM), redistributing population only to identified building footprints and human settlements while masking unpopulated mountainous terrain.
coverage: 2020, entire North Korean landmass at 100m resolution
last_updated_evidence: HTTP Last-Modified: Sun, 20 Sep 2020 00:32:12 GMT; Content-Length: 5,984,373 bytes.
license: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0)
presentation: GeoTIFF format, small file size (~6 MB) due to sparse settlement compression.
build_idea: Run zonal statistics across COD-AB county polygons to produce updated 2020 county populations and generate settlement density heatmap layers.
notes: Because it is only 6 MB, the entire country's 100m population model can be processed in Node.js or Python without high memory overhead.

name: WorldPop North Korea 100m Annual Population Counts 2000-2020
description: Annual 100m resolution gridded population datasets for North Korea for every single year from 2000 through 2020. Generated via Random Forest dasymetric modeling using land cover, lights at night, topography, and infrastructure covariates.
last_updated_evidence: HTTP Last-Modified: Thu, 22 Nov 2018 18:03:58 GMT; Content-Length: 89,126,247 bytes.
license: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0)
presentation: 21 annual GeoTIFF rasters (~89 MB each).
build_idea: Enable time-slider comparisons of rural depopulation and urbanization shifts between 2000 and 2020.
notes: Accessible programmatically via WorldPop REST API at https://hub.worldpop.org/rest/data/pop/wpgp?iso3=PRK.

name: WorldPop North Korea 100m Age & Sex Disaggregated Rasters 2020
description: Gridded 100m rasters disaggregating North Korea's population by sex and 5-year age groups (0, 1, 5, 10, ... 80+) for year 2020. Allows calculating demographic pyramids and dependency ratios for any custom polygon, county, or radius.
last_updated_evidence: HTTP Last-Modified: Tue, 17 Nov 2020 22:39:51 GMT; Content-Length: 3,287,976 bytes per cohort.
license: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0)
presentation: Open directory on WorldPop HTTPS server with direct GeoTIFF downloads (~3.3 MB each).
build_idea: Compute estimated 2020 age-pyramids for each individual North Korean county or prison camp zone.
notes: Files follow naming: prk_f_{age}_2020_constrained.tif and prk_m_{age}_2020_constrained.tif.

name: Kontur Population 400m H3 Hexagon Density for DPRK
description: Population density dataset aggregated into uniform H3 hexagons at resolution 8 (approximately 400m diameter). Built by fusing Global Human Settlement Layer (GHSL), Facebook High Resolution Settlement Layer, Microsoft Building Footprints, and OpenStreetMap data.
last_updated_evidence: HDX package release timestamp 2023-10-31; verified resource kontur_population_KP_20231101.gpkg.gz (3,471,637 bytes).
license: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0)
presentation: Compressed GeoPackage (3.5 MB), containing vector H3 hexagons with population count column.
build_idea: Convert to vector tiles (pbf) for MapLibre to display an ultra-modern 3D hexagon population density extrusion layer across North Korea.
notes: Much lighter and faster to render in MapLibre WebGL than raw raster GeoTIFFs.

name: NASA GIBS VIIRS Black Marble Nighttime Lights WMTS Tile Service
publisher: NASA Earth Science Data and Information System (ESDIS) / GIBS
description: Standard OGC WMTS and WMS tile service streaming Suomi-NPP VIIRS Day/Night Band (DNB) Black Marble composite nighttime imagery. Completely free, public, and keyless, enabling real-time raster map overlay of electricity emissions across the Korean Peninsula.
last_updated_evidence: Verified live tile request (z=6, y=25, x=54) returned HTTP 200 with 63,376 byte PNG from NASA servers.
license: NASA Open Data Policy (Public Domain)
presentation: Directly consumable XYZ/WMTS raster tiles, zero configuration needed in MapLibre.
build_idea: Add a toggleable 'Night Lights / Electricity Proxy' map layer on our site to visually showcase the stark contrast between South Korea/China and North Korea's blackout conditions.
notes: URL template works directly in MapLibre: sources: { 'black-marble': { type: 'raster', tiles: ['https://gibs.earthdata.nasa.gov/wmts/epsg3857/best/VIIRS_Black_Marble/default/2016-01-01/GoogleMapsCompatible_Level8/{z}/{y}/{x}.png'], tileSize: 256 } }.

name: Earth Observation Group VIIRS Nighttime Lights Annual & Monthly Composites
publisher: Payne Institute for Public Policy, Colorado School of Mines
description: Research-grade cloud-free annual and monthly nighttime radiance grids (VIIRS VNL v2.1 and v2.2) filtered for ephemeral lights (fires, aurora) and calibrated in nanowatts/cm²/sr. The primary dataset used by academic economists to estimate regional North Korean GDP.
last_updated_evidence: Annual VNL v2.2 releases cover up through 2024/2025; portal requires free user login token.
license: Open Data with mandatory attribution to Payne Institute EOG
presentation: GeoTIFF raster tiles (tile 75N060E covers Korean Peninsula).
build_idea: Extract county-level mean nighttime radiance to calculate a 2012-2025 electrification trajectory index for each county in North Korea.
notes: Requires free registration account for bulk HTTPS downloads; raw pixel values are floating point radiance.

name: FAO GIEWS Country Brief & Cereal Balance System: DPRK
publisher: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)
description: Continuous monitoring of DPRK agricultural seasons, weather impacts, planting and harvesting progress, cereal production estimates (rice paddy, maize), and national cereal import requirements based on the FAO/GIEWS Country Cereal Balance System (CCBS).
last_updated_evidence: Verified page contents via curl: 'Reference Date: 04-September-2026'; details 2026 main food crop harvesting.
license: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 IGO (CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO)
presentation: Well-written HTML brief with embedded cereal balance tables and production bar charts.
build_idea: Scrape quarterly cereal production and import deficit figures to power a live 'Food Security & Harvest Status' monitor.
notes: Main crops monitored: rice (paddy), maize, wheat, barley, soybeans, and potatoes. Reference date updated September 2026.

name: WFP VAM DPRK Subnational Dekadal Rainfall & Anomalies (CHIRPS)
publisher: World Food Programme (WFP) Vulnerability Analysis and Mapping (VAM)
description: Subnational dekadal (10-day) rainfall indicators derived from CHIRPS v2 infrared satellite precipitation data and CHIRPS-GEFS forecasts, aggregated by administrative units with P-codes. Contains 10-day rainfall, 1-month and 3-month rolling aggregations, long-term averages, and anomaly percentages.
last_updated_evidence: HDX API last_modified timestamp is 2026-09-23T13:28:35; updated every 5 days.
license: Creative Commons Attribution for Intergovernmental Organisations
presentation: Clean CSV tables with standard ADM P-codes for 5-year rolling and full historical archives.
build_idea: Map drought and flooding anomalies by county to explain localized crop failures and food shortages on our interactive map.
notes: Columns: rfh (10-day rain mm), r1h (1-month mm), r3h (3-month mm), rfq (anomaly %), and Pcode.

name: WFP VAM DPRK Subnational Dekadal Vegetation Index (MODIS NDVI)
publisher: World Food Programme (WFP) Vulnerability Analysis and Mapping (VAM)
description: Dekadal Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) from NASA Terra/Aqua MODIS collection 6.1 aggregated across DPRK subnational administrative boundaries. Measures crop health and canopy vigor relative to long-term averages to detect drought impacts.
last_updated_evidence: HDX API last_modified timestamp is 2026-09-23T13:29:56; updated every dekad.
license: Creative Commons Attribution for Intergovernmental Organisations
presentation: CSV tables containing 10-day NDVI (vim), long-term average (vim_lta), and anomaly % (viq).
build_idea: Provide an agricultural health layer: color counties green for healthy vegetation and brown/red for severe agricultural drought.
notes: Links directly to COD-AB boundaries via Pcode column.

name: UNICEF Multiple Indicator Cluster Survey 2017 (MICS6) DPRK Findings Report
publisher: Central Bureau of Statistics, Pyongyang & UNICEF
description: The landmark 2017 MICS survey covering 8,500 households across all 11 provinces of North Korea. Published in June 2018, it is the most authoritative recent health survey, providing provincial tables on child stunting (19.1% national), wasting (2.5%), infant diarrhea, maternal care, clean water access, and iodized salt.
coverage: 2017 survey data, published June 2018, all 11 provinces
last_updated_evidence: Verified official PDF download via curl: HTTP 200, Content-Length: 4,113,875 bytes.
license: UNICEF / Government of DPRK Official Publication
presentation: Comprehensive 246-page PDF report with hundreds of detailed statistical indicator tables disaggregated by province, urban/rural, and wealth quintile.
build_idea: Digitize provincial nutrition tables (stunting and wasting) into a provincial choropleth to demonstrate regional inequality between Pyongyang and northern provinces.
notes: Ryanggang province had the highest child stunting rate (over 32%), compared to Pyongyang's ~10%.

name: WHO Global Health Observatory (GHO) Athena API for DPRK
description: Open OData REST API for global health statistics. Supports filtering by SpatialDim='PRK' to retrieve time series for life expectancy, under-five mortality, maternal mortality, tuberculosis incidence, malaria cases, suicide rates, and healthcare worker densities.
last_updated_evidence: API response verified via curl; records updated August 2, 2024 with life expectancy estimates through 2021/2023.
license: Open access with attribution to WHO
presentation: OData v4 compliant JSON REST API with no authentication required.
build_idea: Build interactive health trend graphs comparing North Korea's tuberculosis burden and life expectancy against regional neighbors.
notes: Indicators include WHOSIS_000001 (life expectancy at birth), MDG_0000000007 (under-five mortality), and TB_e_inc_num (TB incidence).

name: WHO DPRK Compiled Health Indicators Dataset (HDX)
description: Complete compiled CSV release containing 33 indicator category tables for North Korea from the WHO GHO portal, including malaria, tuberculosis, neglected tropical diseases, child mortality, immunization coverage, health workforce, and water/sanitation.
last_updated_evidence: HDX API package last_modified is 2026-09-17T02:29:39; verified 33 distinct CSV resources.
license: Creative Commons Attribution for Intergovernmental Organisations
presentation: Collection of thematic CSV tables on HDX.
build_idea: Bulk-import verified historical health time series into our local SQLite/JSON analytics layer.
notes: Includes world_health_statistics_indicators_prk.csv (6.6 MB) and child_mortality_indicators_prk.csv (1.4 MB).

name: Statistics Korea KOSIS North Korea Portal: Territory & Population (영토/인구)
description: Official South Korean government portal providing 18 harmonized demographic and territorial statistical tables on North Korea, including total population projections to 2070, population density, 5-year age structures, sex ratios, major city populations, and administrative unit counts.
last_updated_evidence: KOSIS live selectTreeData.do response verified: tables updated through 2024/2025; long-term projections to 2070.
license: Open Government Data License Korea (공공데이터 개방)
presentation: Interactive jqGrid web tables on KOSIS and downloadable CSV/XLS; also queryable via selectTreeData.do POST API.
build_idea: Import official ROK government demographic baselines (DT_1ZGA21, DT_1ZGA22, DT_1ZGA15A) to provide historical trendlines and city size comparisons.
notes: Key table IDs: DT_1ZGA15A (administrative names 2014-2024), DT_1ZGA21 (population 2008-2070), DT_1ZGA281 (major cities 1975-2050).

name: Statistics Korea KOSIS North Korea Portal: National Accounts & BOK GDP (국민계정)
description: Official ROK government compilation of 10 statistical tables on North Korea's macroeconomy, including real GDP growth rates (1990-2024), sector-by-sector growth (mining, manufacturing, agriculture), real/nominal GDP in KRW/USD, industrial structure, GNI, and market price index (시장물가지수).
last_updated_evidence: Verified via live probe: DT_1ZGA31 (경제성장률) covers 1990-2024; DT_1ZGG7 (시장물가지수) covers 2006-2024.
license: Open Government Data License Korea (공공데이터 개방)
presentation: HTML and JSON tables on KOSIS with direct CSV export.
build_idea: Build macro charts showing North Korea's economic cycles from post-war expansion through the 1990s collapse and recent sanctions/recovery.
notes: Table DT_1ZGG7 (시장물가지수) provides market price indices from 2006 to 2024, an invaluable proxy for unofficial jangmadang market inflation.

name: Statistics Korea KOSIS North Korea Portal: Agriculture & Food Production (농림수산업)
description: Comprehensive time series of 18 tables on North Korean agricultural performance: food crop production (식량작물 생산량 1965-2025), rice cultivation area by province (시도별 벼 재배면적 2019-2025), agricultural productivity indicators, livestock herds, and timber production.
last_updated_evidence: Table DT_1ZGA532 (시도별 벼 재배면적) verified covering 2019-2025; DT_1ZGA55 covering 1965-2025.
license: Open Government Data License Korea (공공데이터 개방)
presentation: Interactive tables on KOSIS with downloadable CSVs.
build_idea: Render provincial rice cultivation area and annual crop production choropleths to highlight South Hwanghae and South Pyongan as the country's breadbasket.
notes: Data represents the consensus ROK intelligence and agricultural estimate developed by the Rural Development Administration (RDA).

name: Statistics Korea KOSIS North Korea Portal: Health & Social Indicators (보건)
description: Ten statistical tables detailing public health and mortality in North Korea: life expectancy projections (2008-2070), number of physicians and pharmacists (1965-2024), infant mortality, under-five stunting prevalence (DT_BWB0091, 2000-2024), and maternal mortality ratios.
last_updated_evidence: Live selectTreeData.do probe verified table ranges; DT_BWB0091 (발육부진 아동 비율) covers 2000-2024.
license: Open Government Data License Korea (공공데이터 개방)
presentation: Standard KOSIS tabular interface with direct CSV download.
build_idea: Display child stunting and doctor availability alongside health facilities on our living conditions dashboard.
notes: Combines ROK intelligence estimates with harmonized UN inter-agency estimates.

name: Statistics Korea KOSIS North Korea Portal: Energy & Electricity (에너지)
publisher: Statistics Korea (통계청) & Korea Energy Economics Institute
description: Seven statistical tables providing long-term empirical data on North Korea's energy sector: crude oil imports and refining capacity (1980-2024), primary energy supply (열량), electricity generation capacity (발전설비용량), total electricity generated (발전 전력량), and per capita power output.
last_updated_evidence: Verified live via probe_kosis_bukhan.py; all 7 tables updated through 2024.
license: Open Government Data License Korea (공공데이터 개방)
presentation: Interactive web tables on KOSIS.
build_idea: Correlate national electricity output numbers (DT_1ZGA74) directly with nighttime light radiance changes observed by VIIRS satellites.
notes: Shows thermal vs. hydroelectric capacity breakdown; hydroelectric dominance explains the extreme seasonal winter power blackouts.

name: Ministry of Unification North Korea Information Portal: NKMap GIS & Search API
description: Interactive GIS platform and hidden FastAPI backend powering the Ministry of Unification's North Korea map. Provides search and coordinates (Korean TM/GRS80) for hundreds of administrative divisions, factories, theaters, department stores, universities, airports, and monuments with structured attribute cards.
coverage: North Korea nationwide facilities and places
last_updated_evidence: Rebuilt Single Page App using VWorld 3.0 WebGL API; FastAPI search endpoint verified via curl returning 301 items for Pyongyang alone.
license: Open Government Data License Korea
presentation: Modern VWorld WebGL GIS interface, backed by a responsive JSON FastAPI backend.
build_idea: Crawl all city/county names through nkmapSearchFastApi.do to extract coordinates, official North Korean names, area sizes, and facility rosters for our Atlas points of interest.
notes: Coordinates are in Korean Central Belt GRS80 (EPSG:5186) and can be reprojected to WGS84 with proj4js: x_crdnt, y_crdnt.

name: Ministry of Unification: Defectors by DPRK Origin Province (북한이탈주민 재북 출신지역별 현황)
description: Official statistical record of all North Korean defectors who entered South Korea, broken down by their pre-escape home province in North Korea (함경북도, 양강도, 함경남도, 평안남북도, etc.) and sex. Demonstrates that over 75% of defectors originate from northern border provinces.
coverage: 1998-2024 cumulative and annual, all DPRK provinces
last_updated_evidence: Quarterly statistical updates on Unification Ministry portal and data.go.kr; verified CSV dataset on data.go.kr.
license: Open Government Data License Korea (공공데이터 개방)
presentation: CSV download on data.go.kr and quarterly summary reports on unikorea.go.kr.
build_idea: Build a provincial choropleth map of defector origins to visually show which parts of North Korea escape to freedom and where testimonies originate.
notes: Essential context for human rights documentation: explains why outside knowledge of Hamgyong and Ryanggang is far more detailed than Chagang or Hwanghae.

name: Bank of Korea Annual North Korea Real GDP Growth Estimates
description: The gold standard annual macroeconomic assessment of North Korea's economy, published by the Bank of Korea every summer using the UN System of National Accounts (SNA). Provides real GDP growth rates, nominal GNI, per capita income, and sector value-added (agriculture, mining, heavy/light manufacturing, services, utilities).
last_updated_evidence: Official 2025 DPRK GDP estimate press release published July 31, 2026 (+3.5% growth).
license: Public Press Release with Attribution
presentation: Detailed press release PDF with statistical appendix tables, also archived into BOK ECOS database.
build_idea: Feature an annual economic barometer showing growth fluctuations against sanctions regimes, Russia arms trade, and COVID border closures.
notes: 2025 growth was +3.5%, 2024 growth was +3.7%, 2023 growth was +3.1%.

name: Rural Development Administration (RDA) Annual North Korea Crop Production Estimates
description: Annual authoritative South Korean assessment of North Korean agricultural yield released every December. Combines meteorological data from 27 North Korean weather stations, satellite vegetation indices, fertilizer importation trends, and field crop disease surveillance to estimate grain harvests by crop and province.
coverage: Annual releases (1990-2025), North Korea nationwide and provincial
last_updated_evidence: RDA official release published December 2025: 2025 production estimated at 4.90 million tonnes (up 120,000 tonnes from 2024's 4.78M).
license: Open Government Press Release (KOGL Type 1)
presentation: Press release with breakdown tables: rice (2.25M tonnes), maize (1.52M tonnes), wheat/barley (360k), potatoes (550k), soybeans (200k).
build_idea: Update our food security tracker every December with RDA's official harvest numbers and provincial yield maps.
notes: Considered more accurate than official DPRK state announcements because RDA calibrates satellite imagery against known North Korean seed varieties.

name: Korea Rural Economic Institute (KREI): North Korea Agricultural Trends (북한농업동향)
description: Quarterly and biannual periodical providing in-depth analysis of North Korea's agricultural policies, rural grain procurement prices, Sino-DPRK fertilizer and pesticide trade, weather conditions, greenhouse construction, and rural living standards.

name: National Geographic Information Institute (NGII): National Atlas of Korea (북한 행정/인구 지명)
publisher: National Geographic Information Institute, Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport (국토지리정보원)

name: JAXA & MAFF JASMAI: Satellite Agro-Meteorological Monitoring for DPRK
publisher: Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) & Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries (農林水産省)
description: Satellite-based agro-meteorological monitoring system (JASMAI / JASMIN) operated by JAXA and Japan's Ministry of Agriculture. Uses GCOM-W (AMSR2), GPM, and ALOS-2 satellites to track soil moisture, surface temperature, precipitation, and rice crop vegetation indices across East Asia including North Korea.

last_updated_evidence: Operational near-real-time satellite monitoring feed; verified active platform status.

presentation: Interactive WebGIS map and raster download service.

notes: Microwave radiometers penetrate cloud cover during the summer monsoon season, providing soil moisture when optical satellites are blinded by clouds.
